name: Moscow Mule
tagline: Spicy ginger, crisp lime, ice cold.
intro: The Moscow Mule is a quick, fizzy drink that's easy to love: vodka, lime and a generous pour of ginger beer. It's spicy, tart and refreshing, and it needs no shaking. Serve it in a copper mug if you have one.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of a Moscow Mule in a copper mug with lime and mint

glassware.name: Copper mug
glassware.note: A highball glass works just as well. Copper keeps the drink cold.

ingredients.note: A clean, mid-range vodka is all you need.
Squeeze it fresh. It balances the sweetness of the ginger beer.
Choose a spicy ginger beer rather than ginger ale for the proper bite.

steps.title: Chill the mug
steps.body: Fill the mug with ice and let it sit while you gather your ingredients. A cold mug keeps the drink fizzy and cold.

steps.title: Add vodka and lime
steps.body: With the mug full of ice, add the 2 oz of vodka and ½ oz of lime juice.

steps.title: Top with ginger beer
steps.body: Slowly pour in the 4 oz of cold ginger beer, tilting the mug slightly to protect the bubbles.

steps.title: Stir once
steps.body: Give it one gentle stir from the bottom with a bar spoon. One lift is enough to combine without losing fizz.

steps.title: Garnish
steps.body: Squeeze a lime wedge over the top and drop it in, or perch it on the rim. Add a mint sprig if you like the aroma.

tips: Pro tip: Keep your ginger beer well chilled. Warm soda foams up and goes flat fast.
Pro tip: Taste a few ginger beers. They vary from sweet and mild to fiery and dry.
Common mistake: Using ginger ale. It tastes much sweeter and misses the spicy kick.
Common mistake: Pouring the ginger beer too fast, which kills the fizz.

variations.name: Kentucky Mule
variations.description: Swap the vodka for bourbon for a warmer, caramel-toned drink.

variations.name: Dark and Stormy-style Mule
variations.description: Use dark rum in place of vodka for a richer, molasses flavor.

variations.name: Berry Mule
variations.description: Muddle a few raspberries or blackberries in the mug before adding ice.

substitutions: Ginger beer: A spicy ginger ale works in a pinch, but add a little extra lime to keep it balanced.
Copper mug: A chilled highball or Collins glass is a fine substitute.
Vodka: Gin makes a Gin-Gin Mule, with a more herbal edge.
history: The Moscow Mule dates to the early 1940s in the United States, where it helped popularize vodka. Accounts of exactly who invented it and where vary, but they involve a vodka brand, a ginger beer producer and the copper mugs it's now known for.

seo.title: Moscow Mule Recipe: Vodka, Lime and Ginger Beer
seo.description: Make a Moscow Mule with 2 oz vodka, ½ oz lime juice and 4 oz ginger beer. Quick steps, tips and variations for a perfect mule.
